_readme: The complete set of non-app-specific capabilities the factory provides: what it is, which package
owns it, which SEAM INTERFACE (file + symbol + methods) others code against, and who consumes it.
Why it exists: 'every capability' cannot be checked against a list that does not exist. THREE
notification implementations were written because nobody had a place to look that would have said
one already existed. The third is still in the tree -- see violations on `notifications`.
THE ARCHITECTURE THIS ENCODES: packages/core DECLARES the contracts; other packages IMPLEMENT them.
So `seams` are the interfaces a package declares, and `implementsSeams` names contracts declared
elsewhere that it satisfies. v1 of this file pointed every seam at a package barrel file, which
· every packages/* dir on disk has an entry, and every path named here exists
· every declared seam SYMBOL really appears in the file that claims it
· every declared seam METHOD really appears in that interface  [decision item 12]
· consumers verified in BOTH directions against real pubspecs
· no registered seam may be implemented under apps/ unless declared as a violation  [C-3, widened]
VIOLATIONS ARE DECLARED, DATED AND PRINTED ON EVERY RUN. A known gap that nobody sees becomes
permanent. Each names why it is not yet fixed and what would unblock it.

_why: [pipeline C-8] EVERY VENDOR SATISFIES THE PORTABILITY CHECKLIST, not just 'behind a seam'.
Top-down from the charter kept 'behind a seam' and silently dropped the rest -- which is how a
seam ends up LOOKING like portability while a vendor swap still needs a store release.
SIX PARTS, not four. The requirement's own title says 'four-part' and portability-standard.md's
checklist lists SIX; the lock resolved the contradiction to six, the checklist being the primary
record. Four are machine-checkable and BLOCK; two are judgement and PRINT:
1 openProtocol   PRINTS  -- does it speak a standard, or is there a compatibility layer
2 seam           CHECKED -- the named symbol must exist where it claims to
3 configKeyed    CHECKED -- every surface is runtime-config-keyed, or compile-time WITH a
reason. 'No release to repoint' is the property.
4 ownTheRecord   PRINTS  -- the app depends on OUR record, not the vendor's
5 exportPath     CHECKED -- the cited runbook/script must exist on disk
6 exitPlan       CHECKED -- a named alternative and its swap cost, non-empty
SURFACES ARE DERIVED FROM THE TREE, never typed here, and from FOUR sources because any one
alone is blind (all four verified 2026-07-28):
a. `*.fromEnvironment('KEY')` in Dart -- MULTILINE. A line-based grep finds 2 of the 11 that
exist, because dart format wraps the literal onto the next line. UPDATE_URL is one it misses.
b. `interface Env` in services/*/src/types.ts -- REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET lives ONLY here, so
without it RevenueCat, the amendment's own example, is invisible.
c. wrangler `binding` keys AND `ratelimits[].name` -- ratelimits uses `name`, not `binding`, so
a binding-only scan cannot see EVENTS_LIMITER.
d. `triggers.crons` -- a schedule is an external surface too; a dead cron looks like a live one.
Every derived surface must be claimed by exactly one vendor or declared a non-vendor surface.
That is what stops a new vendor arriving unnoticed -- the failure this whole register exists for.
SCOPE: services, not libraries. portability-standard.md's checklist opens 'before adopting any new
SERVICE'. Dart package dependencies are [2]C-5's limb (c), which already stops an app importing a
vendor SDK the seam wraps; duplicating them here would be two lists to keep in step.

supabase.surface: Portfolio-wide identity/auth (project Cross_Platform_Auth) and the Postgres behind it.
supabase.stickiness: ★★★ — portability-standard.md names RLS coupling as one of three sticky points.
supabase.openProtocol: YES — OIDC/JWKS for tokens and plain Postgres underneath. Verification is against standard JWKS claims, not a Supabase SDK call, which is what makes the identity provider swappable.

configKeyed.detail: URL and anon key are dart-defines with compiled-in fallbacks, and the Worker reads SUPABASE_URL from its own env — repointing needs no app release.

supabase.ownTheRecord: YES — entitlements and app state live in OUR D1, keyed on the standard `sub` claim. The app depends on our record, not Supabase's.

exportPath.detail: pg_dump via the Supabase dashboard/API; the schema is plain Postgres with no proprietary types.

exitPlan.alternative: any OIDC provider (Auth0, Clerk, self-hosted Keycloak) behind the same AuthRepository seam
exitPlan.swapCost: Medium — JWKS verification is standard, so the cost is re-issuing sessions and migrating the user table, NOT rewriting the app.

cloudflare.surface: Workers runtime, D1 (platform_db, subly_db), KV (config, JWKS cache), R2 (exports), and the events rate-limiter.
cloudflare.stickiness: ★★★ — portability-standard.md names KV/DO as a sticky point.
cloudflare.openProtocol: PARTIAL — D1 is SQLite dialect and R2 is S3-compatible, both portable. KV and the rate-limiter are proprietary; the crons are a Workers-only scheduler. This is the honest weak spot, and it is why the stickiness is ★★★.

configKeyed.detail: Bindings are wrangler config, not code — swapping a database or bucket is a config edit and a deploy, never an app release.

cloudflare.ownTheRecord: YES — D1 IS our record. The risk here is not losing the record to a vendor, it is the SQLite dialect and the KV semantics.

exportPath.detail: PUBLIC, CHECKABLE EVIDENCE: the D1 schema is plain SQL migrations in this repo — that IS the export shape, and it is why a D1 export lands in any SQLite or Postgres. R2 is S3-compatible so rclone moves it. KV has no bulk export primitive; the mitigation is that KV holds only last-good config and a JWKS cache, both regenerable, so nothing in KV is a record of record. ⬜ FINDING 2026-07-28: the subly-api `EXPORTS` R2 binding is declared in types.ts and referenced NOWHERE in the code — a bound bucket with no writer, the same fail-closed-with-no-open-path shape [2]C-6 exists to catch. Routed to stage 4.

exitPlan.alternative: Postgres/Neon + S3 + any Node host behind the same Worker handlers
exitPlan.swapCost: High for KV/DO semantics, Low for D1/R2. Deliberately kept: nothing durable lives in KV.

revenuecat.surface: Subscription entitlement provider — the client SDK key and the server webhook secret.
revenuecat.stickiness: ★★★★ — payments, the stickiest point the standard names.
revenuecat.openProtocol: NO — payment APIs are proprietary and there is no standard to speak. This is precisely why part 4 carries the weight for this vendor.

configKeyed.detail: Client key is a dart-define with a fallback; the webhook secret is Worker env. Neither requires an app release to rotate.

revenuecat.ownTheRecord: YES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE STRATEGY — entitlements live in OUR table fed by a per-provider adapter, so the payment vendor is swappable even though payment APIs are not. This is the one line the audit note said to carry forward verbatim.

exportPath.detail: Entitlements are ours in D1 and export with it. RevenueCat itself holds no record we depend on.

exitPlan.alternative: Paddle (the locked MoR, ADR 004) or direct store IAP, behind the same entitlement adapter
exitPlan.swapCost: Medium — a new adapter and a webhook, but no app data migration, because we own the record.

revenuecat.note: ⬜ NOT YET LIVE. Nobody can pay NIKATRU today; stage 5 owns the money rail. Recorded now because the surfaces already exist in the tree, and a vendor whose keys are wired before its checklist is exactly the adoption-without-review this requirement stops.

glitchtip.surface: Crash and error reporting sink (self-hostable Sentry-protocol server).
glitchtip.stickiness: ★ — deliberately the least sticky choice available.
glitchtip.openProtocol: YES — speaks the Sentry protocol, so the sentry_flutter SDK talks to it unmodified and any Sentry-protocol sink is a drop-in.

configKeyed.reason: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-27: GLITCHTIP_DSN stays compile-time while UPDATE_URL moves to runtime. A DSN is a build-identity fact — a build reports as itself — and routing crash reports through runtime config would mean a broken config could silently disable the very channel that reports it being broken.

glitchtip.ownTheRecord: N/A — telemetry is a diagnostic stream, not a record the app depends on. Losing history costs insight, never correctness.

exportPath.detail: Self-hosted; the whole instance is ours, and the runbook covers the server backup.

exitPlan.alternative: Sentry SaaS, or any Sentry-protocol server — the DSN is the only thing that changes
exitPlan.swapCost: Low — one config value, because the protocol is open.

_why: Derived surfaces that are NOT third-party services. They still have to be classified, or an
unclaimed token would be indistinguishable from a vendor nobody reviewed.
A surface here may still carry a VIOLATION -- see UPDATE_URL, which is a decided fix, not a
judgement call.
nonVendorSurfaces.ALLOWED_ORIGINS: our own domains — the CORS allowlist, guarded by assert-cors-allowlist.mjs
nonVendorSurfaces.APP_VERSION: build metadata — injected at build time, deliberately not read from package_info_plus
nonVendorSurfaces.SKIP_REMOTE_CONFIG: test/demo switch, no external system behind it
nonVendorSurfaces.UPDATE_URL: where the force-update wall sends users. FIXED 2026-07-28 — it was compile-time only, which made the kill-switch circular: the one thing the wall must do in an emergency is send users somewhere, but its destination was frozen at build time, so redirecting it meant shipping the very build the wall exists to replace. Now `AppConfig.updateUrl` in the RUNTIME config (core), read by the brick's app.dart with the compiled-in define as the offline fallback. This guard is what caught it; the owner decision of 2026-07-27 is what settled it.
nonVendorSurfaces.E2E_EMAIL: throwaway CI test credential — e2e.yml provisions a pre-confirmed user before the run and purges it after, so this names no durable external account
nonVendorSurfaces.E2E_PASSWORD: throwaway CI test credential — see E2E_EMAIL

_why: [pipeline C-4] A PACKAGE IS EARNED, NEVER NAMED. 39-CHASSIS §2 adjudicated this and it was
written nowhere that binds. A capability name is not a reason: followed loosely, the remaining
gap list would spawn packages for share, deep-links, review, purchases, connectivity and
analytics -- six pubspecs, six analysis_options, six workspace entries, six test harnesses and
six CI surfaces, forever, for one founder. Applied correctly, share_plus / app_links /
in_app_review all land in the existing platform_storage.
Keyed by PACKAGE, not capability, because two capabilities can share one package (core owns
both `core` and `analytics_funnel`) and the cost being controlled is the package.
THE ENUM IS CLOSED and each reason must SUBSTANTIATE ITSELF AGAINST THE TREE -- free text was
rejected at lock time because a justification nobody can check is a justification that always
passes:
native-binary    evidence.dependency must be declared in that package's own pubspec
licence-exposure evidence.dependency must be declared, and evidence.licence named
codegen          evidence.buildFile must exist on disk
GRANDFATHERED    predates the rule; needs declaredOn + detail, and PRINTS on every run
Rejections already adjudicated, recorded so no future session re-litigates them: do NOT rename
platform_storage -> platform_adapters, and do NOT merge notifications into it. Both were built
under the older reading; the rename is churn across every pubspec and import for zero
user-visible value.

packages/auth_supabase.detail: Ships platform code: the secure-storage bridges and the deep-link/callback handling that completes an OAuth redirect, which differ on all six targets. It is also the ONLY package permitted to import the Supabase SDK — [2]C-5 limb (c) fails the build for any app that reaches for it directly, which is what keeps the identity provider swappable.

packages/platform_storage.detail: Keychain on iOS/macOS, KeyStore on Android, DPAPI on Windows, libsecret on Linux -- five different native implementations behind one Dart call. This is the shape that earns a package: the platform difference is real and somebody must absorb it once.

packages/notifications.detail: Native scheduling APIs per platform, and the capability genuinely differs per platform (Linux shows but cannot schedule; Windows on the pinned 17.x does neither; web has no plugin at all) -- which is why NotificationCapabilities exists at all.

packages/telemetry.detail: Ships native crash handlers -- a Dart-only reporter cannot catch a native crash, which is the class of failure this package exists for.

packages/tokens.detail: A build step, not a library: style-dictionary compiles the token source into sites/_shared/assets/tokens.css, and ci.yml's `tokens` lane rebuilds and fails on any diff. It has no pubspec because it is a Node package.

packages/core.detail: The spine, not an earned split -- it is what the other packages are separate FROM, so the earn test does not really apply to it. Substantiates none of the three (crypto and cryptography are both pure Dart). Left grandfathered rather than given an invented reason: an exemption you can see is safer than a justification that is not true.

packages/design_system.detail: Pure Flutter widgets -- no native payload, no licence exposure, no codegen. Its real justification is the C-5 boundary (it must not be able to see the domain), which is a boundary argument rather than one of the three structural reasons. Recorded honestly instead of stretching the enum to fit.

packages/api_client.detail: dio is pure Dart, so this substantiates nothing. It is the single most likely package to be MERGED if the rule is ever applied retroactively -- kept because [2]C-3 has just moved all three dio transports into it and moving them twice would be churn.

packages/analysis.detail: A lint ruleset -- config, not code, and flutter_lints is not a native payload. It is nonetheless the one grandfathered package with a clear reason to stay separate: [2]C-12 made it the single convention set that every package, every app and the brick template inherits, so one rule edit reaches every app the factory will ever stamp. (Until 2026-07-28 it had ZERO consumers and its own include sat commented out, which is why this entry originally read 'delivers nothing'.)

capabilities.capability: The app-neutral spine: it DECLARES most of the factory's seam contracts, and owns config, caches and domain models. Nothing here may know about a specific app.

missingMethods.decision: 00-RECONCILIATION-DECISIONS.md PART 2.2 item 12 — "NotificationService tap surface: stage 2, named seam method in C-1's register"
missingMethods.why: The seam can schedule and cancel but has no way to DELIVER a tap back to the app, so a scheduled reminder cannot open anything. The analytics half already exists and is stranded: AnalyticsFunnel.onNotificationOpened(String kind) at apps/subly/lib/state/analytics_funnel.dart can RECORD a tap that nothing can report. A reminder nobody can act on is the dead-feature shape C-6 exists to catch.

capabilities.capability: HTTP transport to the shared platform Worker — config, consent and analytics event delivery.
capabilities.note: Gained its first real consumers at 5f3466b when [2]C-3 moved all three dio transports here out of apps/subly and the brick.

capabilityMatrix.degradesOn: Web is a different network stack: CORS is enforced by the browser and only fixable SERVER-side, User-Agent cannot be set and the assignment is silently IGNORED, and certificate pinning is impossible because the page never sees the socket. Uses its own HttpPlatform enum rather than TargetPlatform because this package is pure Dart and declares no Flutter dependency.

capabilities.capability: Identity: sign-in/up, OAuth redirect, session and bearer token, and the CLIENT half of account deletion. The only package that imports the Supabase SDK.
capabilities.note: [2]C-15, 2026-07-28. Before this the ONLY implementations lived inside apps/subly, so the brick wired no auth and no tokenProvider — every stamped app was born unable to authenticate. Ships SupabaseAuthRepository, a REAL InMemoryAuthRepository (wired, not mocked — a stub returning null from everything is the fail-closed shape [2]C-6 exists to catch), SecureSessionStorage (G-43: the SDK defaults to plaintext shared_preferences for the access AND refresh tokens), and AuthCapabilities, the declared six-platform matrix with Linux SUPPORTED — the contrary claim was checked against pub.dev and is false. `DELETE /v1/account` is stage 4's route: the client half refuses loudly rather than pretending to have deleted anything.

violations.detail: Subly's own Supabase implementation, plus a direct `package:supabase_flutter` import in its main.dart. NOT A NEW DEFECT — it is the SAME code that C-15 has now given a shared home. Until 2026-07-28 it was a HOMELESS sole implementation, which [2]C-3's lock explicitly routed here; creating packages/auth_supabase is what makes it detectably a fork, and the guards said so the moment the package landed. That is the register working, not a regression.
violations.blockedBy: 39-CHASSIS cut 1 froze apps/subly as a legacy rail-prover. Deleting or moving this reverses an agreed cut, which the standing authorization does not cover — declared rather than moved, exactly as the notifications fork and the three adapter bypasses were.

violations.detail: Subly's mock. Superseded by InMemoryAuthRepository in packages/auth_supabase, which is a real implementation rather than a mock — it signs in, holds a session, emits on authStateChanges, expires and signs out.

capabilityMatrix.degradesOn: Web has no OS keychain for a page, so the session is NOT OS-backed; the OAuth token arrives in the URL FRAGMENT (query parsing fails silently) and the flow must be a full-page redirect, never a popup. Linux IS supported — the contrary claim was checked against pub.dev and is false.

capabilities.capability: Shared widgets and theming. Deliberately domain-free — the lock DECISION stays with the caller so this package never learns what a paywall is ([2]C-5 boundary).
capabilities.noSeamReason: A widget library, not a contract — callers use the widgets directly. The one decision that COULD have become a seam (what to lock) is deliberately left with the caller so this package never learns domain vocabulary: that is [2]C-5's boundary, and PaywallGate is the example.

capabilities.capability: Secure-token and key-value storage across all six platforms.

capabilityMatrix.degradesOn: Linux secure storage is CONDITIONAL ON THE ENVIRONMENT: libsecret must be installed AND a Secret Service daemon running and unlocked. Headless, kiosk and CI sessions often have neither, so a write can fail at runtime where every other desktop succeeds. Web is not OS-backed at all.

capabilities.note: Wired into Subly at 5f3466b. Until then the only app in production had NO crash reporting: the package existed, passed 8 tests, and shipped to nobody.

capabilityMatrix.degradesOn: Dart errors report everywhere, but NATIVE crashes only on Android/iOS/macOS. On desktop Windows and Linux a segfault or OOM kill produces NO report — which is exactly what a user means by "it just closed". Collapsing the two is how a portfolio believes it has crash reporting and does not.

capabilities.note: Deliberately NOT given to apps/subly, which 39-CHASSIS cut 1 froze as a legacy rail-prover. That freeze is why the FLN 17.x pin stays there.

violations.detail: A third, independent implementation: its own `class NotificationService` singleton calling flutter_local_notifications 17.x directly, and importing Subly's own Subscription model. This is the exact fork [2]C-1's audit note cites as the reason the register exists.
violations.blockedBy: 39-CHASSIS cut 1 froze apps/subly as a legacy rail-prover. Deleting this fork reverses an agreed cut, which the standing authorization does not cover — owner decided 2026-07-28 to declare it rather than move it.

capabilityMatrix.degradesOn: Linux shows but cannot schedule (zonedSchedule unimplemented in 17.x-19.x); Windows can do neither on 17.x (support landed in 18.x); web and fuchsia neither. Unsupported calls no-op so a caller falls back to an in-app nudge.

capabilities.capability: The portfolio-wide conversion funnel: launch, activation, paywall viewed, checkout started, purchase success/failed, notification opened. Entirely app-neutral — it names no Subly concept.

violations.detail: Lives inside an app despite being app-neutral, so no other app or stamped brick can emit the funnel. [5]M-16 already records that four of its methods (onPaywallViewed, onCheckoutStarted, onPurchaseSuccess, onPurchaseFailed) have ZERO callers — the analytics rail emits everything except the money.
violations.fixOwner: 00-RECONCILIATION-DECISIONS.md PART 2.2 item 15 — "C-1 assigns an owning package". Assigned here to packages/core, beside the Analytics seam it wraps.
violations.blockedBy: Moving it edits apps/subly, frozen by 39-CHASSIS cut 1. Owner decided 2026-07-28 to declare the assignment now and move it in [2]C-3's increment.

capabilities.noSeamReason: A concrete funnel over the Analytics seam that core already declares; it adds no contract of its own. Callers use it directly.

capabilities.capability: The shared analysis ruleset — the one convention set every package and stamped app should inherit.
capabilities.note: ✅ [2]C-12 WIRED IT 2026-07-28. It previously had ZERO consumers — including its own analysis_options.yaml, where the include sat inside a COMMENT, so the package's only mention of the mechanism it exists to provide was not code. Score was 0 of 10: every analysis_options.yaml in the tree included flutter_lints or lints directly. All eight non-exempt files now inherit it, each with the dev_dependency that makes the include resolve. The two exempt files are the shared set itself and the package's own self-apply, which uses a relative include so the lint package can analyze itself before the workspace resolves. Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-lint-inheritance.mjs — which also asserts the set still ESCALATES a rule to `error`, because inheritance at default severity prints and ships (measured: analyze exits 0).

capabilities.capability: Design tokens built by style-dictionary into sites/_shared/assets/tokens.css, which the websites serve.
capabilities.unconsumedReason: A Node package with no pubspec.yaml, so the Dart-consumer test cannot apply. Its real consumer is sites/_shared/assets/tokens.css, gated by ci.yml's `tokens` lane which rebuilds and fails on any diff. 39-CHASSIS cut 3's 'zero consumers, delete it' premise was falsified 2026-07-26 — recorded as SUPERSEDED BY FACTS rather than executed blindly.

cloneTells._why: [pipeline C-10] limb 2. Domain vocabulary that belongs to ONE app's problem, not to the chassis. MUST NOT BE EMPTY -- an empty list passes everything silently, which is the failure this repo has hit repeatedly. App NAMES are derived from apps/ on disk, never listed here, so they cannot go stale.
